steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Bollywood is the Hindi-language film industry based in Mumbai, producing more films annually than Hollywood and characterised by musical numbers, melodrama and family-centred narratives.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Nollywood is the Nigerian film industry, one of the largest in the world by output, known for low-budget direct-to-video productions that reflect local cultures and social issues.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Chinese cinema encompasses mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan, with a history spanning martial arts cinema, Fifth Generation art films and contemporary blockbuster productions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: World film industries differ from Hollywood in their production contexts, funding models, distribution networks and relationships with domestic audiences.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name specific film industries and, where possible, specific films as examples rather than making general statements about world cinema. Compare global film industries with Hollywood to demonstrate understanding of different production, distribution and exhibition contexts. Use the correct terminology: Bollywood refers specifically to Hindi-language cinema from Mumbai, not all Indian cinema. When discussing Nollywood, emphasise its unique distribution model and rapid production process rather than judging it against Hollywood budgets. Consider both the cultural significance and the industrial realities of global film industries in your answers.
